verses.text: Di word of di Lord come to me again, say,
“You, son of man, take up lamentation over Tyre,
and talk to Tyre, ‘You wey dey for di entry of di sea, wey be merchant of di peoples to many coastlands, di Lord God talk like dis: Tyre, you don talk, “I dey perfect for beauty.”
Your borders dey for di heart of di seas. Your builders don perfect your beauty.
Dem don make all your planks of fir trees from Senir. Dem don take cedar from Lebanon to make masts for you.
Of di oaks of Bashan dem don make your oars. Dem don make your benches of ivory inlaid for boxwood, from di coasts of Kittim.
Fine linen with embroidered work from Egypt na your sail, to be your banner. Blue and purple from di coasts of Elishah na your awning.
Di inhabitants of Sidon and Arvad na your rowers. Your wise men, Tyre, dey inside you. Dem na your pilots.
Di elders of Gebal and her wise men dey inside you, your caulkers. All di ships of di sea with dem mariners dey inside you, to deal in your merchandise.
Persia and Lud and Put dey for your army, your men of war. Dem hang shield and helmet for you. Dem set forth your glory.
Di men of Arvad with your army dey on your walls round about, and men of Gammad dey for your towers. Dem hang dem shields on your walls round about. Dem don perfect your beauty.
Tarshish na your merchant by reason of di multitude of all kinds of riches. Dem trade silver, iron, tin, and lead for your wares.
Javan, Tubal, and Meshech, dem na your traders. Dem trade persons of men and vessels of bronze for your merchandise.
Dem of di house of Togarmah trade horses and war horses and mules for your wares.
Di men of Dedan na your traders. Many coastlands na market of your hand. Dem bring you for payment horns of ivory and ebony.
Syria na your merchant by reason of di multitude of your handiwork. Dem trade emeralds, purple, embroidered work, fine linen, coral, and rubies for your wares.
Judah and di land of Israel, dem na your traders. Dem trade wheat of Minnith, pannag, honey, oil, and balm for your merchandise.
Damascus na your merchant for di multitude of your handiwork, by reason of di multitude of all kinds of riches, wine of Helbon, and white wool.
Vedan and Javan trade from Uzal for your wares. Wrought iron, cassia, and calamus dey for your merchandise.
Dedan na your trader for precious cloths for riding.
Arabia, and all di princes of Kedar, dem na di traders of your hand. For lambs, and rams, and goats, for dis things dem na your traders.
Di merchants of Sheba and Raamah, dem na your merchants. Dem trade for your wares di chief of all spices, and all precious stones, and gold.
Haran, Canneh, Eden, di merchants of Sheba, Asshur and Chilmad, na your merchants.
Dem na your merchants for choice wares, wrapped in blue and embroidered work, and for chests of rich clothing, bound with cords and made of cedar, among your merchandise.
Di ships of Tarshish na your caravans for your merchandise. You dey replenished, and dey very glorious for di heart of di seas.
Your rowers don bring you into great waters. Di east wind don break you for di heart of di seas.

Your riches, your wares, your merchandise, your mariners, and your pilots, your caulkers, and di dealers for your merchandise, and all your men of war wey dey inside you, with all your company wey dey for your middle, go fall into di heart of di seas for di day of your ruin.
At di sound of di cry of your pilots di suburbs go shake.
All wey handle di oar, di mariners, and all di pilots of di sea, go come down from dem ships. Dem go stand on di land,
and go cause dem voice to dey heard over you, and go cry bitterly. Dem go cast up dust on dem heads. Dem go wallow for ashes.
Dem go make demselves bald for you, and gird dem with sackcloth, and dem go weep for you with bitterness of soul, with bitter mourning.
For dem wailing dem go take up lamentation for you, and lament over you, saying, “Who be like Tyre, like her wey dey destroyed for di middle of di sea?
When your wares go out from di seas, you fill many peoples. You enrich di kings of di earth with di multitude of your riches and of your merchandise.
For di time wey you dey broken by di seas, for di depths of di waters, your merchandise and all your company don fall inside you.
All di inhabitants of di coastlands dey astonished at you, and dem kings dey horribly afraid. Dem faces dey troubled.
Di merchants among di peoples hiss at you. You don become terror, and you no go dey again forever.”’”
Di word of di Lord come to me again, say,

“Son of man, talk to di prince of Tyre, ‘Di Lord God talk like dis: Because your heart dey lifted up, and you don talk, “I be god. I sit for di seat of God, for di middle of di seas,” yet you be man, and no be God, though you set your heart as di heart of God.
See, you dey wiser pass Daniel. No secret dey wey dem fit hide from you.
By your wisdom and by your understanding you don get riches for yourself, and don get gold and silver into your treasuries.
By your great wisdom and by your trade you don increase your riches, and your heart dey lifted up because of your riches,
therefore di Lord God talk like dis: Because you don set your heart as di heart of God,
therefore see, I go bring strangers on you, di terrible of di nations. Dem go draw dem swords against di beauty of your wisdom, and dem go defile your brightness.
Dem go bring you down to di pit. You go die di death of dem wey dey slain, for di heart of di seas.
You go still talk before am wey kill you, “I be God”? But you go be man, and no God, for di hand of am wey wound you.
You go die di deaths of di uncircumcised by di hand of strangers, because I don speak am,’ talk di Lord God.”
Di word of di Lord come to me, say,
“Son of man, take up lamentation over di king of Tyre, and talk to am, ‘Di Lord God talk like dis: You na di seal of perfection, full of wisdom, and perfect for beauty.

You dey for Eden, di garden of God. Every precious stone na your covering: ruby, topaz, and diamond, beryl, onyx, and jasper, sapphire, turquoise, and emerald, and gold. Di workmanship of your settings and your sockets dey prepared for you for di day wey you dey created.
You be di anointed cherub wey cover, and I set you dere. You dey for di holy mountain of God. You waka up and down for di middle of di stones of fire.
You dey perfect for your ways from di day wey you dey created, until unrighteousness dey found inside you.

By di multitude of your trade dem fill di middle of you with violence, and you sin. Therefore I don cast you as profane out of di mountain of God. I don destroy you, covering cherub, from di middle of di stones of fire.
Your heart dey lifted up because of your beauty. You don corrupt your wisdom by reason of your brightness. I don cast you to di ground. I don lay you before kings, so that dem go see you.

By di multitude of your iniquities, for di unrighteousness of your trade, you don profane your sanctuaries. Therefore I don bring fire out of di middle of you. E don devour you, and I don turn you to ashes on di earth for di sight of all wey see you.
All wey know you among di peoples dey astonished at you. You don become terror, and you no go dey again forever.’”
Di word of di Lord come to me, say,
“Son of man, set your face toward Sidon, and prophesy against her,

and talk, ‘Di Lord God talk like dis: See, I dey against you, Sidon, and I go dey glorified for di middle of you. Dem go know say I be di Lord, when I don execute judgments inside her, and don dey sanctified inside her.
Because I go send pestilence into her, and blood into her streets. Di wounded go fall for di middle of her, with di sword on her on every side. Dem go know say I be di Lord.
No more go dey pricking brier to di house of Israel, nor painful thorn from all wey dey round about dem, wey despise dem. Dem go know say I be di Lord God.’”

Di Lord God talk like dis: “When I don gather di house of Israel from di peoples among whom dem dey scattered, and don dey sanctified inside dem for di sight of di nations, den dem go dwell for dem own land wey I give to my servant Jacob.

Dem go dwell securely inside am. Yes, dem go build houses, and plant vineyards. Dem go dwell securely, when I don execute judgments on all wey despise dem round about dem. Den dem go know say I be di Lord dem God.”
For di tenth year, for di tenth month, for di twelfth day of di month, di word of di Lord come to me, say,
“Son of man, set your face against Pharaoh king of Egypt, and prophesy against am, and against all Egypt.

Speak, and talk, ‘Di Lord God talk like dis: See, I dey against you, Pharaoh king of Egypt, di great monster wey lie for di middle of im rivers, wey don talk, “My river na my own, and I don make am for myself.”

I go put hooks for your jaws, and I go cause di fish of your rivers to stick to your scales. I go bring you up out of di middle of your rivers, with all di fish of your rivers wey stick to your scales.

I go leave you thrown into di wilderness, you and all di fish of your rivers. You go fall upon di open field. You no go dey brought together, nor gathered. I don give you for food to di animals of di earth and to di birds of di sky.
All di inhabitants of Egypt go know say I be di Lord, because dem don be staff of reed to di house of Israel.
When dem take hold of you by your hand, you break, and tear all dem shoulder. When dem lean on you, you break, and make all dem loins to stand.
Therefore di Lord God talk like dis: See, I go bring sword on you, and cut off from you man and animal.
Di land of Egypt go be desolation and waste. Dem go know say I be di Lord, because e don talk, “Di river na mine, and I don make am.”
Therefore see, I dey against you, and against your rivers, and I go make di land of Egypt waste and desolate, from Migdol to Syene, even to di border of Cush.
No foot of man go pass through am, nor foot of animal go pass through am. E no go dey inhabited 40 years.

I go make di land of Egypt desolation for di middle of di countries wey dey desolate, and her cities among di cities wey dey waste go dey desolation 40 years. I go scatter di Egyptians among di nations, and disperse dem through di countries.
For di Lord God talk like dis: At di end of 40 years I go gather di Egyptians from di peoples where dem dey scattered.
I go bring again di captivity of Egypt, and cause dem to return into di land of Pathros, into di land of dem birth. Dem go dey dere a base kingdom.
E go be di basest of di kingdoms. E no go exalt imself any more above di nations. I go diminish dem, so that dem no go rule over di nations.
E no go be di confidence of di house of Israel any more, bringing iniquity to remembrance, when dem turn to follow dem. Dem go know say I be di Lord God.’”
E happen for di 27th year, for di first month, for di first day of di month, say di word of di Lord come to me, say,

“Son of man, Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon cause im army to serve great service against Tyre. Every head dey made bald, and every shoulder dey rubbed raw. Yet e get no wages, nor im army, from Tyre, for di service wey e serve against am.

Therefore di Lord God talk like dis: ‘See, I go give di land of Egypt to Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon. E go carry away her multitude, and take her plunder, and take her prey. E go be di wages for im army.
I don give am di land of Egypt for im labour wey e labour, because dem work for me,’ talk di Lord God.
‘For dat day I go cause di horn of di house of Israel to bud, and I go give you opening of di mouth for di middle of dem. Dem go know say I be di Lord.’”
Di word of di Lord come to me again, say,
“Son of man, prophesy, and talk, ‘Di Lord God talk like dis: Howl, “Woe for di day!”
Because di day dey near, even di day of di Lord dey near. E go be cloudy day, di time of di nations.
Sword go come on Egypt, and anguish go dey for Cush, when di slain dey fall for Egypt, and dem take away her multitude, and her foundations dey broken down.
Cush, and Put, and Lud, and all di mixed people, and Cub, and di people of di land wey dey in league, go fall with dem by di sword.’
Di Lord talk like dis: ‘Dem wey uphold Egypt go fall. Di pride of her power go come down. From Migdol to Syene dem go fall in am by di sword,’ talk di Lord God.
‘Dem go dey desolate for di middle of di countries wey dey desolate, and her cities go dey among di cities wey dey waste.
Dem go know say I be di Lord, when I don set fire for Egypt, and all her helpers dey destroyed.
For dat day messengers go go out from me in ships to make di careless Ethiopians afraid. Anguish go dey on dem, as for di day of Egypt, because see, e dey come.’
Di Lord God talk like dis: ‘I go also make di multitude of Egypt to cease by di hand of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon.
E and im people with am, di terrible of di nations, go dey brought to destroy di land. Dem go draw dem swords against Egypt, and fill di land with di slain.
I go make di rivers dry, and sell di land into di hand of evil men. I go make di land waste, and all wey dey inside am, by di hand of strangers. I, di Lord, don speak am.’
Di Lord God talk like dis: ‘I go also destroy di idols, and cause di images to cease from Memphis. No prince go dey again from di land of Egypt, and I go put fear for di land of Egypt.
I go make Pathros desolate, and set fire for Zoan, and execute judgments on Thebes.
I go pour my wrath on Sin, di stronghold of Egypt, and I go cut off di multitude of Thebes.
I go set fire for Egypt. Sin go dey in great anguish. Thebes go dey broken up. Memphis go get enemies for daytime.
Di young men of On and of Pi Beseth go fall by di sword, and dem go go into captivity.
For Tehaphnehes di day go dey withdrawn, when I break di yokes of Egypt dere, and di pride of her power go cease inside her. As for her, cloud go cover her, and her daughters go go into captivity.
Thus I go execute judgments on Egypt. Dem go know say I be di Lord.’”
E happen for di eleventh year, for di first month, for di seventh day of di month, say di word of di Lord come to me, say,
“Son of man, I don break di arm of Pharaoh king of Egypt. See, e no dey bound up to dey healed, by putting on bandage to bind am, so that e go dey strong to hold di sword.”
Therefore di Lord God talk like dis: “See, I dey against Pharaoh king of Egypt, and I go break im arms, di strong arm, and di one wey dey broken. I go cause di sword to fall out of im hand.
I go scatter di Egyptians among di nations, and disperse dem through di countries.
I go strengthen di arms of di king of Babylon, and put my sword for im hand. But I go break Pharaoh arms, and e go groan before am with di groaning of one wey dey mortally wounded.

I go hold up di arms of di king of Babylon, but di arms of Pharaoh go fall down. Dem go know say I be di Lord, when I put my sword into di hand of di king of Babylon, and e go stretch am out on di land of Egypt.
I go scatter di Egyptians among di nations, and disperse dem through di countries. Dem go know say I be di Lord.”
For di eleventh year, for di third month, for di first day of di month, di word of di Lord come to me, say,
“Son of man, speak to Pharaoh king of Egypt, and to im multitude: ‘Who you dey like for your greatness?
See, Assyria na cedar for Lebanon, with beautiful branches, and with forest shade, and of high stature, and im top dey among di thick boughs.
Di waters nourish am. Di deep make am grow tall, with im rivers waka round about im plantation, and e send out im channels to all di trees of di field.
Therefore im stature dey exalted above all di trees of di field. Im boughs multiply, and im branches become long because of many waters, when e shoot forth.
All di birds of di sky make dem nests for im boughs. Under im branches all di animals of di field bring forth dem young. For im shade all great nations dwell.
So e dey beautiful for im greatness, for di length of im branches, because im root dey by many waters.
Di cedars for di garden of God no fit hide am. Di fir trees no dey like im boughs, and di plane trees no dey like im branches. No tree for di garden of God dey like am for im beauty.
I don make am beautiful by di multitude of im branches, so that all di trees of Eden, wey dey di garden of God, envy am.’
Therefore di Lord God talk like dis: ‘Because e don lift up imself for stature, and e don set im top among di thick boughs, and im heart dey lifted up for im height,
I don deliver am into di hand of di mighty one of di nations. E go surely deal with am. I don drive am out for im wickedness.

Strangers, di terrible of di nations, don cut am off, and don leave am. Upon di mountains and for all di valleys im branches don fall, and im boughs don dey broken by all di watercourses of di land. All di peoples of di earth don go down from im shade, and don leave am.
Upon im ruin all di birds of di sky go dwell, and all di animals of di field go dey upon im branches,

so that none of di trees by di waters go exalt demselves for dem stature, neither set dem top among di thick boughs, neither dem trees stand up for dem height, all wey drink water, because dem all dey delivered to death, to di lower parts of di earth, among di children of men, with dem wey go down to di pit.’

Di Lord God talk like dis: ‘For di day wey e go down to Sheol I cause mourning. I cover di deep for am. I restrain di rivers, and di great waters dey stopped. I cause Lebanon to mourn for am, and all di trees of di field faint for am.

I make di nations shake at di sound of im fall, when I cast am down to Sheol with dem wey descend into di pit. All di trees of Eden, di choice and best of Lebanon, all wey drink water, dey comforted for di lower parts of di earth.
Dem also go down into Sheol with am to dem wey dey slain by di sword, yes, dem wey be im arm, wey dwell under im shade among di nations.

To who you dey like so for glory and for greatness among di trees of Eden? Yet you go dey brought down with di trees of Eden to di lower parts of di earth. You go lie among di uncircumcised, with dem wey dey slain by di sword. Dis na Pharaoh and all im multitude,’ talk di Lord God.”
E happen for di twelfth year, for di twelfth month, for di first day of di month, say di word of di Lord come to me, say,

“Son of man, take up lamentation over Pharaoh king of Egypt, and tell am, ‘You dey like young lion of di nations. Yet you be like monster for di seas. You break forth with your rivers, and trouble di waters with your feet, and foul dem rivers.’
Di Lord God talk like dis: ‘I go spread out my net over you with assembly of many peoples, and dem go bring you up for my net.
I go leave you on di land. I go cast you out on di open field, and I go cause all di birds of di sky to settle on you, and I go fill di animals of di whole earth with you.
I go lay your flesh on di mountains, and fill di valleys with your height.
I go also water di land wey you swim with your blood, even to di mountains. Di watercourses go dey full of you.
When I extinguish you, I go cover di heavens, and make di stars of am dark. I go cover di sun with cloud, and di moon no go give im light.
All di bright lights of heaven I go make dark over you, and set darkness on your land,’ talk di Lord God.
‘I go also trouble di hearts of many peoples, when I bring your destruction among di nations, into di countries wey you no know.

Yes, I go make many peoples dey amazed at you, and dem kings go dey horribly afraid for you, when I brandish my sword before dem. Dem go tremble at every moment, everyone for im own life, for di day of your fall.’
Because di Lord God talk like dis: ‘Di sword of di king of Babylon go come on you.
By di swords of di mighty I go cause your multitude to fall. Dem all na di terrible of di nations. Dem go bring to nothing di pride of Egypt, and all im multitude go dey destroyed.
I go also destroy all di animals of am from beside many waters. Di foot of man no go trouble dem any more, nor di hoofs of animals trouble dem.
Den I go make dem waters clear, and cause dem rivers to run like oil,’ talk di Lord God.
‘When I don make di land of Egypt desolate and waste, di land wey dey empty of all wey full am, when I strike all wey dwell inside am, den dem go know say I be di Lord.’
Dis na di lamentation wey dem go lament. Di daughters of di nations go lament am. Dem go lament for Egypt, and for all im multitude,” talk di Lord God.
E happen also for di twelfth year, for di 15th day of di month, say di word of di Lord come to me, say,
“Son of man, wail for di multitude of Egypt, and cast dem down, even am, and di daughters of di famous nations, to di lower parts of di earth, with dem wey go down into di pit.
Wetin you dey pass for beauty? Go down, and dey laid with di uncircumcised.
Dem go fall among dem wey dey slain by di sword. She dey delivered to di sword. Draw am away with all im multitudes.
Di strong among di mighty go talk to am out of di middle of Sheol with dem wey help am. Dem don go down. Dem lie still, di uncircumcised, slain by di sword.
Asshur dey dere and all her company. Her graves dey round about am. All of dem dey slain, fallen by di sword.
Her graves dey set for di uttermost parts of di pit, and her company dey round about her grave. All of dem dey slain, fallen by di sword, wey cause terror for di land of di living.

Elam dey dere and all her multitude round about her grave. All of dem dey slain, fallen by di sword, wey go down uncircumcised into di lower parts of di earth, wey cause dem terror for di land of di living, and dem bear dem shame with dem wey go down to di pit.

Dem don set her bed for di middle of di slain with all her multitude. Her graves dey round about am. All of dem dey uncircumcised, slain by di sword, because dem terror dey caused for di land of di living, and dem bear dem shame with dem wey go down to di pit. E dey put for di middle of di slain.
Meshech, Tubal and all her multitude dey dere. Her graves dey round about am. All of dem dey uncircumcised, slain by di sword, because dem cause dem terror for di land of di living.

Dem no lie with di mighty wey don fall of di uncircumcised, wey go down to Sheol with dem weapons of war, and don lay dem swords under dem heads. Dem iniquities dey upon dem bones, because di terror of di mighty dey for di land of di living.
But you go dey broken for di middle of di uncircumcised, and go lie with dem wey dey slain by di sword.
Edom dey dere, her kings and all her princes, wey for dem might dey laid with dem wey dey slain by di sword. Dem go lie with di uncircumcised, and with dem wey go down to di pit.

Di princes of di north dey dere, all of dem, and all di Sidonians, wey go down with di slain, with dem terror. Dem dey ashamed of dem might. Dem lie uncircumcised with dem wey dey slain by di sword, and bear dem shame with dem wey go down to di pit.
Pharaoh go see dem, and go dey comforted over all im multitude, Pharaoh and all im army, slain by di sword,” talk di Lord God.
“Because I don cause im terror for di land of di living, e go dey laid among di uncircumcised, with dem wey dey slain by di sword, even Pharaoh and all im multitude,” talk di Lord God.
Di word of di Lord come to me, say,
“Son of man, speak to di children of your people, and tell dem, ‘When I bring sword on land, if di people of di land take one man from among dem, and set am as dem watchman,
if when e see di sword come on di land, e blow di trumpet, and warn di people,
den whoever hear di sound of di trumpet, and no take warning, if di sword come, and take am away, im blood go dey on im own head.
E hear di sound of di trumpet, and no take warning. Im blood go dey on am. But im wey take warning go deliver im soul.

But if di watchman see di sword come, and no blow di trumpet, and di people no dey warned, and sword come, and take any person from among dem, dat man dey taken away for im iniquity, but im blood I go require at di watchman hand.’
So you, son of man, I don set you watchman to di house of Israel. Therefore you go hear di word from my mouth, and warn dem from me.
When I talk to di wicked, ‘Wicked man, you go surely die,’ and you no speak to warn di wicked from im way, dat wicked man go die for im iniquity, but im blood I go require at your hand.
Nevertheless, if you warn di wicked of im way to turn from am, and e no turn from im way, e go die for im iniquity, but you don deliver your soul.
You, son of man, talk to di house of Israel: ‘Una talk like dis: “Our transgressions and our sins dey on us, and we dey pine away for dem. How den we go live?”’

Tell dem, ‘As I live,’ talk di Lord God, ‘I no get pleasure for di death of di wicked, but say di wicked turn from im way and live. Turn una, turn una from una evil ways! Because why una go die, house of Israel?’

You, son of man, talk to di children of your people, ‘Di righteousness of di righteous no go deliver am for di day of im transgression. As for di wickedness of di wicked, e no go make am fall for di day wey e turn from im wickedness. Di righteous no fit live by im righteousness for di day wey e sin.’

When I talk to di righteous, say e go surely live, if e trust for im righteousness, and commit iniquity, none of im righteous deeds go dey remembered. For im iniquity wey e don commit, e go die for am.
Again, when I talk to di wicked, ‘You go surely die,’ if e turn from im sin, and do wetin dey lawful and right,
if di wicked restore di pledge, give again wetin e don rob, waka for di statutes of life, committing no iniquity, e go surely live. E no go die.
None of im sins wey e don commit go dey remembered against am. E don do wetin dey lawful and right. E go surely live.
Yet di children of your people talk, ‘Di way of di Lord no dey equal,’ but as for dem, dem way no dey equal.
When di righteous turn from im righteousness, and commit iniquity, e go die inside am.
When di wicked turn from im wickedness, and do wetin dey lawful and right, e go live by am.
Yet una talk, ‘Di way of di Lord no dey equal.’ I go judge una, house of Israel, everyone after im ways.”
E happen for di twelfth year of our captivity, for di tenth month, for di fifth day of di month, say one wey don escape from Jerusalem come to me, saying, “Di city don dey struck.”
Now di hand of di Lord dey on me for di evening, before di one wey escape come. E open my mouth until e come to me for di morning. My mouth dey opened, and I no dey mute again.
Di word of di Lord come to me, say,
“Son of man, dem wey inhabit dem waste places for di land of Israel dey talk, saying, ‘Abraham dey one, and e inherit di land. But we dey many. Di land dey given to us for inheritance.’
Therefore talk to dem, ‘Di Lord God talk like dis: Una eat with di blood, and lift up una eyes to una idols, and shed blood. Una go possess di land?
Una stand on una sword. Una work abomination. Everyone defile im neighbour wife. Una go possess di land?’

Talk to dem like dis: ‘Di Lord God talk like dis: As I live, surely dem wey dey di waste places go fall by di sword, and im wey dey di open field I go give to di animals to dey devoured, and dem wey dey di strongholds and for di caves go die of di pestilence.
I go make di land desolate and waste, and di pride of her power go cease. Di mountains of Israel go dey desolate, so that none go pass through.
Den dem go know say I be di Lord, when I don make di land desolate and waste because of all dem abominations wey dem don commit.’

As for you, son of man, di children of your people dey talk against you by di walls and for di doors of di houses, and dem dey speak to each other, everyone to im brother, saying, ‘Come, I beg una, and hear wetin be di word wey come from di Lord.’

Dem come to you as people dey come, and dem sit before you as my people, and dem hear your words, but dem no do dem, because with dem mouth dem show much love, but dem heart go after dem dishonest gain.
See, you be to dem like one wey sing love songs with beautiful voice, and play well on instrument. Dem hear your words, but dem no do dem.
When dis come to pass (see, e go come), den dem go know say prophet don dey among dem.”
Di word of di Lord come to me, say,

“Son of man, prophesy against di shepherds of Israel. Prophesy, and talk to dem, even to di shepherds, ‘Di Lord God talk like dis: Woe to di shepherds of Israel wey feed demselves! Di shepherds no suppose feed di sheep?
Una eat di fat, and una clothe una with di wool. Una kill di fatlings, but una no feed di sheep.
Di diseased una no strengthen, neither una heal di sick, neither una bind up di broken, neither una bring again di strayed, neither una seek di lost. But una rule dem with force and with severity.
Dem dey scattered, because no shepherd dey, and dem become food to all di animals of di field, and dem dey scattered.
My sheep wander through all di mountains, and upon every high hill. Yes, my sheep dey scattered on all di surface of di earth, and nobody search or seek.’
Therefore, una shepherds, hear di word of di Lord:

‘As I live,’ talk di Lord God, ‘surely because my sheep don become prey, and my sheep don become food to every animal of di field, because no shepherd dey, neither my shepherds search for my sheep, but di shepherds feed demselves, and no feed my sheep,
therefore, una shepherds, hear di word of di Lord:

Di Lord God talk like dis: See, I dey against di shepherds. I go require my sheep at dem hand, and cause dem to cease from feeding di sheep. Di shepherds no go feed demselves any more. I go deliver my sheep from dem mouth, so that dem no go be food for dem.’
Because di Lord God talk like dis: ‘See, I, even I, go search for my sheep, and seek dem out.

As shepherd seek out im flock for di day wey e dey among im sheep wey dey scattered, so I go seek out my sheep. I go deliver dem out of all di places where dem don dey scattered for di cloudy and dark day.

I go bring dem out from di peoples, and gather dem from di countries, and go bring dem into dem own land. I go feed dem upon di mountains of Israel, by di watercourses, and for all di inhabited places of di country.
I go feed dem with good pasture, and dem fold go dey upon di mountains of di height of Israel. Dere dem go lie down for good fold. Dem go feed for fat pasture upon di mountains of Israel.
I go feed my sheep, and I go cause dem to lie down,’ talk di Lord God.

‘I go seek dat wey dey lost, and bring again dat wey dey driven away, and bind up dat wey dey broken, and strengthen dat wey dey sick. But di fat and di strong I go destroy. I go feed dem with justice.
As for una, my flock, di Lord God talk like dis: See, I judge between sheep and sheep, between di rams and di male goats.

E dey small thing to una say una don feed on di good pasture, but una must tread down with una feet di rest of una pasture? And say una don drink of clear waters, but una must foul di residue with una feet?
As for my sheep, dem eat wetin una don tread with una feet, and dem drink wetin una feet don foul.’
Therefore di Lord God talk like dis to dem: ‘See, I, even I, go judge between di fat sheep and di lean sheep.
Because una push with side and with shoulder, and thrust all di diseased with una horns, until una don scatter dem abroad,
therefore I go save my flock, and dem no go be prey any more. I go judge between sheep and sheep.
I go set up one shepherd over dem, and e go feed dem, even my servant David. E go feed dem, and e go be dem shepherd.
I, di Lord, go be dem God, and my servant David go be prince among dem. I, di Lord, don speak am.
I go make with dem covenant of peace, and cause di evil animals to cease from di land. Dem go dwell securely for di wilderness, and sleep for di woods.
I go make dem and di places round about my hill blessing. I go cause di shower to come down for im season. Dem go be showers of blessing.

Di tree of di field go yield im fruit, and di earth go yield im increase. Dem go dey secure for dem land. Dem go know say I be di Lord, when I don break di bars of dem yoke, and deliver dem out of di hand of those wey make slaves of dem.
Dem no go dey prey to di nations any more, neither di animals of di earth go devour dem. But dem go dwell securely, and none go make dem afraid.
I go raise up for dem plant of renown, and dem no go dey consumed with hunger for di land any more, neither bear di shame of di nations any more.
Dem go know say I, di Lord dem God, dey with dem, and say dem, di house of Israel, na my people,’ talk di Lord God.
‘Una my sheep, di sheep of my pasture, na men, and I be una God,’ talk di Lord God.”
Moreover di word of di Lord come to me, say,
“Son of man, set your face against Mount Seir, and prophesy against am,
and talk to am, ‘Di Lord God talk like dis: See, Mount Seir, I dey against you, and I go stretch out my hand against you, and I go make you desolate and waste.
I go lay your cities waste, and you go be desolate. Una go know say I be di Lord.
Because you don have perpetual enmity, and don give over di children of Israel to di power of di sword for di time of dem calamity, for di time of di iniquity of di end,
therefore, as I live,’ talk di Lord God, ‘I go prepare you for blood, and blood go pursue you. Since you no hate blood, therefore blood go pursue you.
Thus I go make Mount Seir waste and desolate, and I go cut off from am di one wey pass through and di one wey return.
I go fill im mountains with im slain men. For your hills, and for your valleys, and for all your watercourses, dem go fall wey dey slain by di sword.
I go make you perpetual desolations, and your cities no go be inhabited. Una go know say I be di Lord.
Because you don talk, “Dis two nations and dis two countries go be mine, and we go possess dem,” though di Lord dey dere,

therefore, as I live,’ talk di Lord God, ‘I go do according to your anger, and according to your envy, wey you don use out of your hatred against dem. I go make myself known among dem, when I judge you.
You go know say I, di Lord, don hear all your blasphemies wey you don speak against di mountains of Israel, saying, “Dem dey desolate. Dem dey given to us to devour.”
You don magnify yourselves against me with your mouth, and don multiply your words against me. I don hear am.’
Di Lord God talk like dis: ‘While di whole earth rejoice, I go make you desolate.
As you rejoice over di inheritance of di house of Israel, because e dey desolate, so I go do to you. You go be desolate, Mount Seir, and all Edom, even all of am. Dem go know say I be di Lord.’”
